profiles.meeting_scenario: A coordination meeting between a community paediatrics neurodevelopment pathway lead and a local authority SEND implementation manager in an English children’s services partnership. The partnership is preparing to relaunch its joint referral pathways for suspected ADHD, developmental coordination disorder (DCD), and autism before the start of the new school half-term, after a prolonged rewrite involving health, education, and therapy services. The old pathway materials already exist and most agencies believe the content is settled, so this meeting is framed as a practical alignment check rather than a decision-making session. The agenda is to confirm readiness for next week’s launch milestone, align on what schools should submit through the single front door, confirm that everyone is working from the same January pathway text, and clarify how updates to the pack will be handled after launch. The expected outcome is apparent agreement that the pathway will go live next week, schools will submit complete referrals through the shared route, the January version is the basis for use, and each side knows its immediate follow-up actions.

members.name: Dr. Aisha Rahman
members.role: Consultant Community Paediatrician and Clinical Lead for Neurodevelopmental Pathways
members.expertise: Neurodevelopmental assessment pathways, NHS triage thresholds, cross-agency clinical governance
members.background: Aisha leads redesign of ADHD, DCD, and autism referral routes across two boroughs, working with community paediatrics, therapy services, CAMHS interfaces, and local authority partners to reduce duplicate referrals and make triage more consistent.
members.private_state: She wants the relaunch date to hold because NHS teams have already been told to expect the revised pathway next week, and she is concerned that reopening practical questions will trigger another delay and prolong pressure on waiting lists.
hidden_assumptions: If colleagues agree the pathway goes live next week, that means services begin working to the revised pathway from that date even if some outward-facing communications catch up shortly after.

A complete referral means complete enough for safe triage: the core referral form, parent concerns, and school information are present, while some pathway-specific evidence can follow after initial acceptance.

When people refer to the January version or January agreed text, they mean the steering-group-approved wording circulated after the 18 January meeting, regardless of later formatting or packaging changes.
If the local authority team is holding the pack, they will maintain the master assembled document for external use and fold in any later clinical wording changes that health sends across.

members.name: Helen Morris
members.role: SEND Service Manager for Education Inclusion
members.expertise: School-facing SEND implementation, SENCO communications, multi-agency rollout planning
members.background: Helen manages the local authority interface with schools, educational psychology, and inclusion services, and is responsible for turning joint pathway decisions into materials that SENCOs can use consistently without repeated clarification.
members.private_state: She wants to avoid a messy rollout that generates avoidable school queries in the first half-term, because her team is stretched and has recently been criticized for issuing guidance before materials felt stable and classroom-ready.
hidden_assumptions: If the pathway goes live next week, that means next week is the point at which schools can be told to start using the revised pathway because the outward-facing pack is stable enough to issue.
A complete referral means complete at the point of submission from the school side, with the evidence set listed in the pack already assembled so schools are not asked to resend material.
When people refer to the January version or January agreed text, they mean the late-January publication-ready pack on SharePoint that reflects the wording as schools will actually see it.

If her team is holding the pack, that means they maintain the school-facing wrapper and briefing note, while health remains responsible for editing, formatting, and reissuing the clinical forms and pathway text when content changes.

misalignment_points.topic: What 'go live next week' actually commits them to
misalignment_points.surface_form: Both agree that the pathway will 'go live next week.'
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 means the revised pathway becomes operational for receiving and handling referrals next week within services, even if some external communications and packaging details continue to settle immediately afterward.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 means next week is when schools can confidently be instructed to start using the revised pathway because the externally issued materials are stable and ready for normal use.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: The phrase is discussed only as a launch milestone rather than unpacked into operational versus external-readiness mechanics, so each hears an ordinary implementation date and assumes the other is using the same standard meaning.

misalignment_points.surface_form: Both agree that schools should send a 'complete referral' through the single front door.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 means complete enough for clinical triage to make a safe routing decision: the referral form, parent views, and school information are present, while additional disorder-specific material can be requested later.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 means complete enough from the school submission side that the evidence listed in the pack has already been gathered and attached before it is sent.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: Both are trying to reduce bounced referrals and use the same familiar phrase from pathway documentation, but one applies a triage sufficiency standard while the other applies a front-end submission quality standard.

misalignment_points.topic: Which 'January version' is being treated as settled
misalignment_points.surface_form: Both refer to 'the January version' or 'the January agreed text' as the basis for launch.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 is thinking of the wording circulated after the 18 January steering-group meeting, which she regards as the agreed substantive pathway text used for NHS briefing.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 is thinking of the late-January publication pack on SharePoint that she regards as the settled January version because it is the school-facing form in which the pathway will be issued.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: Both artifacts come from the same January sign-off cycle and are casually referenced by month rather than exact filename, and because the substantive content overlaps heavily, neither expects they may be anchoring on different concrete documents.

misalignment_points.topic: Who edits the master pack after launch
misalignment_points.surface_form: Both agree that Helen's team will 'hold the pack' and Aisha's team will 'send over any clinical updates.'
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 assumes the local authority team will act as custodian of the assembled master pack used externally, incorporating later clinical wording edits sent by health into the maintained pack.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 assumes her team will only update the school-facing wrapper and circulate whatever revised clinical documents health itself edits and reissues, without taking responsibility for altering the clinical master files.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: The conversation frames this as a light-touch maintenance arrangement after launch, so 'hold the pack' sounds like an innocuous admin shorthand rather than a discussion about who actually performs document editing and reassembly.
